newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares down 2.7 pct despite sharp recovery.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares down 2.7 pct despite sharp recovery.

text.p: Istanbul shares on Friday recovered some of their extremely sharp early losses but still closed well down amid mounting political concerns, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed 44 points, or 2.7 percent lower at 1,583, after rebounding from an early afternoon low of 1,534 which was down 5.72 percent from Thursday.
Trade volume shrank further to 17.16 trillion lira from Thursday's 20.91 trillion and Wednesday's 22.73 trillion.
The index dived 5.2 percent this week after jumping 4.6 percent last week when the market was dominated by technical factors rather than the political agenda.
It had surged 8.7 percent the previous week on hopes that an alternative alliance would be formed to oust the ruling Islamist Welfare Party from power.
Brokers said players would be tuned to political developments in coming days.

"It was normal that reaction buys followed the extremely sharp falls earlier in the day. But caution remained ahead of the weekend. It may move either way depending on news to emerge from Ankara," said Kadri Isik from Halk securities.

Coalition partners agreed to hand over the premiership from Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan to his junior conservative ally Tansu Ciller, a senior MP from Ciller's True Path Party said late on Thursday.

The pair announced on June 1 that they would seek parliament approval for snap polls with a caretaker government to be headed by Ciller to overcome a dispute between the government and the secularist army over growing religious activism.
However, the coalition now has 274 seats in 550-member parliament and relies on support from a small rightist party to pass an alteration in government and an early election law.
The coalition has been troubled by disputes and defections over religious activism since the army called in February for a crackdown on Moslem revivalism.

Of the 244 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 173 to 34 and 37 were steady. The IMKB Industrial sank 1.91 percent to 1,490, IMKB Services dived 2.78 percent to 1,571 and IMKB Financial plunged 3.74 percent to 1,723.

Actives were led by largely state-owned oil refiner Tupras, down 6,000 lira at 71,000, flat steel giant Eregli, up 250 lira at 18,750 and utility Cukurova Elektrik, down 10,000 lira at 210,000. They made up about 21 percent of the total turnover.
